text:
maria: Hey -- just noticed a weird $98.40 charge on my corp card from 'AIRPORT-RIDE' while I was waiting at SFO yesterday. receipt PDF uploaded but it only shows a flat total and no itemization. Is surge accepted on corpcard?
lee (Finance): Hi Maria — thanks for flagging. We need the itemized receipt showing the fare + surge breakdown or a note from the driver/ride vendor. If not available, manager approval can be an exception.
maria: I uploaded receipt: https://files.company/receipts/2051234567-sfo-ride.pdf. It literally says "Total: $98.40" and merchant code RIDE-SVC. No breakdown.
sarah (Manager): I approve the exception for Maria for this trip to SFO. Business reason: onsite customer kickoff, flight delay caused 45min wait. @lee (Finance) — ok to process? :thumbsup:
lee (Finance): Thanks @sarah. Can you reply here with "approved" so we have thread copy for audit? Also Maria, please file the expense in Expensify with project code RW-ONBOARD and attach the PDF and this thread.
maria: Approved — filing now. Quick Q: is the surge portion VAT reclaimable for our UK entity? This was a US ride but we sometimes see VAT on EU rides.
lee (Finance): For US domestic rides VAT/GST typically doesn't apply. If there had been VAT charged and a valid VAT invoice, we'd reclaim for UK entity, but for US vendors no. If you ever have an EU ride with VAT shown, upload the invoice and tag "VAT" in Expensify and we'll review.
expensify-bot: Expense created (ID: 342-205123) by maria for $98.40, status: submitted.
lee (Finance): Got it. We'll mark this as approved exception and reimburse once the expense is in approved state in Expensify. Note for records: manager approval saved in thread. Closing here. :white_check_mark:
